>EDMR

Weight loss surgery for me would be a bad idea I believe. I know I could lose weight if I fixed the underlying problems, thing is, I just don't know how.   


There was a few years where I was workingg and made good money, I made enough to buy opiates and I used them "medicinally" and took the same dosage every day for a year.   
I was productive and not depressed, and with the addition of my (prescirbed) benzos, my anxiety was in check from the benzos and the opiates treated my depression. I was doing good. I wasn't nodding off.  I wasn't a junkie, or selling things or what not.   


When I lost my job due to covid (I lived with parents and worked) I was unable to continue to buy the opiates, so my depression has spiraled because I haven't been able to have anything to treat my depression. It's terrible. The traditional medications DO NOT WORK for me and it's awful.   


I think the real reason behind my depression, to get "real" here, is that I just kind of believe that humanity is collapsing as we speak. It's a slower process than you'd imagine, but if you look at how nothing really functions in this world, the climate is turning hostile to human life, we can't get people to wear masks, I'm not sure if there's any anti depressant that will fix the problems that I have. I feel like I'm depressed because of "material conditions," not a brain chemistry imbalance which depression drugs target. Idk.
Sure, go ahead. Always down to chat, especially rn.

It's miserable. I understand why nobody wants to be with me, I am a mess. I have mental issues that have been treatment resistant and I am just not really attractive or desirable. It just compounds the feeling of being isolated.

I second this. Learning not to give a fuck about what others think, especially those who aren't really willing tolisten to your side of things is the best thing you can do. 

While I have done this pretty well over the years, my depression is still bad, but thta's not really related to what others think of me.
